newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold in Chinese supermarkets venture.
newsitem.headline: Ahold in Chinese supermarkets venture.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV said on Thursday it had agreed on a 50-50 joint venture with China Venturetech Investment Corp (CVIC).
"The new company will start off with the joint operation of 15 supermarkets in Shanghai, currently operated by Zhonghui Supermarkets," the Dutch retailer said in a statement.

Ahold said the new jointly owned company, which will be named Shanghai Ahold-Zhonghui Supermarket Co Ltd, plans to expand considerably in the coming years with an investment of about $50 million. It now employs 600 people.
CVIC, which is majority-owned by the Chinese State Science and Technology Commission and the Finance Ministry, operates more than 30 supermarkets in China.
Over the next few months some of the 15 outlets of the new joint venture will be remodelled to TOPS supermarkets, the store format Ahold uses for its supermarkets across Asia.
Ahold said partner CVIC was known for its innovative approach towards business and added the acquisition was in line with Ahold's strategy to become a major food retailer in Asia.
Ahold has repeatedly said it planned to boost its interests in the Far East.
Currently the bulk of its sales is generated in Europe and the U.S. but recently it has also set up business in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
Last week, Dutch newspapers said Ahold was about to strike a deal with CVIC.
